# Category

Use `Category` for one label from a bounded vocabulary: a country, product
family, customer tier, or class. Use [Set](set.qmd) for multiple labels,
[Hash](hash.qmd) for identifier equality, and [Text](text.qmd) for word meaning.

```yaml
merchant_category: grocery
fraud: false
```

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model(
    d_model=64, n_layers=2, n_heads=4,
    merchant_category=rf.Category(size=128, topk=[3, 10]),
    fraud=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

## Input and options

Accepts scalar Boolean, integer, floating-point, string, or binary labels.
Keep one compatible Arrow type family per field; normalize inconsistent labels
upstream. A null is a [value state](../core-concepts/data-types.qmd#value-state),
not a vocabulary member.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `1024` | Positive vocabulary capacity; `capacity` is also accepted. Embedding and decoder tables grow with it. |
| `p_unavailable` | `0.01` | Training probability of replacing known valued **input** content with unavailable content. Reconstruction targets are unchanged. |
| `topk` | `[]` | Sorted, unique accuracy cutoffs satisfying `1 < k < size`; also controls prediction candidates. |

Capacity counts real labels only. Do not reserve an extra class for null or
unavailable values. See [shared leaf options](../core-concepts/data-types.qmd#shared-leaf-options)
for reconstruction and embedding configuration.

## Vocabulary and learning

Pristine training observations add labels until capacity is full. Validation,
test, and prediction reuse the learned mapping. The mapping is shared with
encoding workers and synchronized for DDP; checkpoints preserve it.

See [Online Vocabulary](../core-concepts/vocabulary.qmd) for admission order,
capacity limits, worker synchronization, and reuse during fine-tuning.

An unknown label stays `valued` but contributes zero categorical content to
the encoder. Its internal sentinel is not an extra embedding row or decoder
class. Known labels contribute learned content plus their state embedding.

Reconstruction uses unweighted state and categorical cross entropy. Class
frequencies remain observable through `counts`, but do not silently change
the probability objective. Training scores the full capacity, including
unpopulated slots. Unavailable valued targets have no categorical loss or
gradient: an unknown answer does not imply a uniform distribution over known
answers. State supervision is retained.

For each reconstruction objective, epoch metrics separate coverage from quality:

| Metric suffix | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `targets.known`, `targets.unavailable` | Counts of selected valued targets inside and outside the vocabulary. |
| `coverage.content` | Known targets divided by all selected valued targets. |
| `accuracy.content`, `accuracy.topK` | Correct predictions among known targets, using populated candidates. |
| `accuracy.all` | Correct predictions divided by all selected valued targets; unavailable answers count as wrong. |
| `nll.content` | Unweighted negative log likelihood over populated candidates, matching written probabilities. |
| `loss.content` | Unweighted categorical training objective over the full capacity, averaged over known targets. |

Names include the field address and stage, for example
`record.merchant_category/validate.coverage.content`. Counts and sums aggregate
across batches and ranks before division. With no known targets, conditional
accuracy, NLL, and content loss are `NaN`, not zero; coverage and all-target
accuracy are zero when selected valued targets exist. With no selected valued
targets, coverage and all-target accuracy are also undefined.

This intentionally replaces the earlier frequency-weighted objective and
uniform-target OOV penalty. Existing checkpoints retain their learned weights;
loading one does not recalibrate it. Continued fitting uses the new objective.

For an application-supplied trained `model`:

```python
labels = rf.Category.vocabulary(model, "record/merchant_category")
counts = rf.Category.counts(model, "record/merchant_category")
```

`vocabulary` returns a tuple snapshot in index order; `counts` returns pristine
valued training exposures, excluding nulls, unavailable values, unused slots,
and the smoothing prior. Repeated epochs count again; DDP counts synchronize
at epoch end. `vocabulary` also accepts a preprocessor's `encoding_context`.
Consult it for inference preprocessing only: training preprocessing occurs
before new labels are reserved.

## Prediction

`content` contains `value`, `probability`, and `topk`. The candidate list has
up to `max(topk)` entries, capped by the populated vocabulary; it is empty
when no cutoffs are configured. Labels are written as `large_string`.

Probabilities are renormalized over **populated labels**, excluding unused
capacity and the unavailable sentinel. An empty vocabulary yields a null best
label and probability zero. Confidence is not an unknown-label detector.
With only one populated label, its conditional probability is one even before
learning; vocabulary membership is not evidence of predictive competence.
Unweighted cross entropy removes a systematic class-weighting distortion, but
does not guarantee calibration under finite data or distribution shift.
See the [prediction envelope](../guides/prediction-output.qmd) for shared state
probabilities, `inferred`, and repeated shapes.
